inputs.original_text: They’re packaging a frightening airport incident as an ICE-agent-hero story, with DHS itself releasing the video. That framing conveniently shifts attention from why a family was stuck in a crowded TSA line to the agency’s preferred image of its agent rushing in. The clip may show a real emergency, but it doesn’t prove the official narrative is the whole story; the release feels designed to steer public attention and manage perceptions of ICE.
inputs.modified_text: DHS releasing the video is the giveaway: they want everyone focused on the ICE agent as a hero, not asking why a family was left in a crowded TSA line in the first place. The emergency may have been real, but that doesn’t make the agency’s version complete. This looks like carefully managed optics—use a frightening moment to polish ICE’s image and bury the questions they don’t want people asking.
